title: L&T Technology Services Ltd - 540115 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: LTTS Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2.7% QoQ in constant currency to $317.1M, with EBIT margin at 16.3%, ahead of its mid-16% aspiration.
summary.overview: Revenue reached $317.1M (up 2.7% QoQ and 4.8% YoY in constant currency, continuing operations), and INR 3,040 crore (up 3.4% QoQ, 12.1% YoY). EBIT margin widened 60 bps QoQ to 16.3%, and management said the mid-16% aspiration was reached a couple of quarters early. Large deal TCV was $203M with over 50% AI-led, and management said the USD100M shortfall from last quarter's target would be recovered over Q3 and Q4. Reported net income of INR 548 crore included a one-time INR 165 crore gain from the SWC divestment, which is now complete.

financial_highlights.change: +53.7% QoQ; +66.8% YoY; includes INR 165 crore one-time SWC gain
vs 77 days in Q1; guided range 80 to 85 days
vs INR 3,394 crore at end Q1

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: Revenue up 2.3% QoQ, with growth from Auto North America, Aero and Rail, and Trucks and Off-highway. Auto Europe remained muted; management expects it to recover next year. Auto is about 50% of Mobility revenue. Margin 16.9%.

segments.name: Sustainability
segments.commentary: Up 13.4% YoY and 4.9% QoQ; now about 30% of revenue per the CFO (38% per the later AI-revenue answer, which conflicts). Nearly half of Q2 large deal wins were here. Margin 29.5%. Management says it is on track for another double-digit growth year.

segments.name: Tech
segments.commentary: Described as stable. Tech Infra and Semcon were strong, Media steady. A global telecom equipment AI program began ramping this quarter. Margin 12%, up 50 bps QoQ. Management expects Tech to be muted in Q3, with Medtech recovery in Q4.

segments.name: Engineering Intelligence (EI)
segments.commentary: Annualized EI-led revenue of $120M in Q2, which management said is about 9.5% of revenue. Headcount was 24,035 and more than 16,000 engineers were upskilled in AI. Over 50% of Q2 large deal wins were AI-led.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 revenue expected to be better than H1, both QoQ and YoY, per management.
Near-term EBIT margin expected around mid-16% levels; aspiration to maintain it.
Long-term aspiration: 13% to 15% revenue CAGR with 16% to 17% EBIT margin over 3 to 5 years.
Wage hike effective Q3, expected impact of 50 to 80 bps on margin; margin guidance stated as inclusive of this.
Effective tax rate guided at 26% to 26.5%.
Management expects to recover the roughly USD100M shortfall from the prior quarter in Q3 and Q4 to keep a USD200M-per-quarter deal pace.
Tech expected muted in Q3; Medtech growth expected from Q3 or Q4; Systems and Platforms growth to accelerate from Q4.
capex_capacity: Set up a dedicated Data Center Engineering business line covering AI infrastructure, servers, storage, ODMs and OEMs.
Launched a new EI lab with NVIDIA for physical AI applications across manufacturing, robotics and supply chain.
Investment in Munich and an EI center to target European auto work.
Headcount rose marginally from 23,845 in Q1 to 24,035 in Q2.
demand_pricing: Large deal TCV of $203M across segments in Q2, with over 50% AI-led. Order backlog and pipeline both up YoY; pipeline up more than 25% YoY.
Offshore mix 55.9%; fixed-price mix 35.6%, rising toward higher-value and outcome-based engagements.
Average deal tenures have lengthened slightly. Management cited roughly 5 to 7 years for a $100M deal, 4 to 5 years for $50M, about 3 years for $25M.
Management says it charges a premium for AI-led work but declined to quantify AI-led margins by service line.
Rupee realized at 95.9 per dollar in Q2, depreciating 1.09% QoQ.
Europe auto remains weak; management said there is little Middle East exposure in oil and gas.

qa_highlights.question: How has Sustainability volatility come down, and how much revenue is long-term?
qa_highlights.answer: Management split Sustainability into four areas (Oil and Gas/Chemicals, FMCG, Energy Automation, Industrial Machinery and Building Tech), built digital twin and AI solutions, and said large deals from last year are now converting to revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Middle East situation affecting oil and gas or overall business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Middle East business is very small and it is not seeing significant impact; work is focused on the US and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Will European auto recover next year, and is it an industry-wide turnaround?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Europe auto to stabilize in the next 6 to 9 months and grow again in 9 to 12 months, as European OEMs rebase and India-based providers replace local vendors. Auto Europe is about 50% of the auto portion of Mobility, and the company does not quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DSO of 78 days comfortable, or is there room to improve it?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company is comfortable at 78 days, well below the 80 to 85 day guided range, and expects to operate around this level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the SWC divestment affect the reported numbers, and what is the run rate from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the INR 165 crore was a one-time gain. From Q3 only continuing operations will be reported, with the SWC operating line of about $36M excluded.

qa_highlights.question: Why are clients converting deals to revenue now, and what changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to AI capex across chips, software, industrials, telecom and infrastructure, clients focusing on growth rather than cost cuts, and LTTS being 9 to 12 months ahead of peers on AI, which it says is gaining share.

qa_highlights.question: What are sustainable margins, and what is the Q4 exit margin?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said near-term margins should be taken at around mid-16% EBIT, with levers from mix, AI and productivity, net of the wage hike. Management did not give a Q4 exit margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wage hike impact, and what does H2 growth mean?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the wage hike in Q3 would have a 50 to 80 bps margin impact. Management said H2 will be better than H1 both QoQ and YoY, without a quarterly number.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the $120M annualized EI revenue was recognized in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the $120M is annualized, so about $30M per quarter. Most AI deal wins have not yet gone into operation, and the company will report AI-led revenue quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI-led revenue defined, and what is its profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: AI revenue counts deliverables where a significant part is created using the AI stack. Management declined to quantify AI-led profitability, but said AI is a margin lever.

risks_watch: Auto Europe remains muted and may need write-offs before recovery; management's recovery timing is 6 to 12 months.
Tech is expected to be muted in Q3 and Medtech recovery is pushed to Q3 or Q4 after a major program ramp-down.
Wage hike of 50 to 80 bps in Q3 may pressure margins if growth lags.
H2 growth acceleration depends on converting the USD100M-plus deal backlog; most AI deal wins are not yet operational.
Middle East escalation could affect oil and gas demand if it persists, per management's own caveat.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and deal momentum, with specific H2 commitments, but cautious on Auto Europe and Tech. Management declined to quantify AI-led margins and quarterly guidance, and hedged the Medtech recovery timing.
key_quotes: EBIT margins improved 60 bps quarter -on-quarter to 16.3%, delivering ahead of timeline on our aspiration for mid-16% EBIT levels.
I'm confirming to you that H2 will be better year-on-year and quarter-to-quarter than H1, sequentially as well as year-on-year, right?
Near term, you should take it to be at these levels, around mid-16% EBIT levels.
We will make sure that we get you the extra USD100 million in Q3 and Q4 because we want to keep to that 200 million pace.

adds.what: Dedicated Data Center Engineering business line (AI infrastructure, servers, storage, ODMs/OEMs) - organizational setup, not physical capacity
Investment in Munich and an EI center to target European auto work

growth.why: Management reiterated a 13-15% revenue CAGR aspiration over 5 years and said H2 FY27 will beat H1 on QoQ and YoY basis, backed by Q2 large-deal TCV of $203M (over 50% AI-led), pipeline up over 25% YoY, and a planned ~$100M recovery in Q3-Q4; no physical capacity additions were quantified.
